findings.failure_path: Verified intervals are merged only within (first, last). If a read of lines 1 through N stops inside row k and a read of lines k through N resumes at the next byte of that row, the two bodies can cover the entire canonical skill. Each range still sees only part of row k, so the bridge withholds the Skill event and the checkpoint can fire after a complete read.
findings.smallest_fix: Translate verified spans to absolute canonical offsets and combine coverage for the same skill across range headers, preserving the row-separator rule. Add a two-range regression that loads with contiguous coverage and fails with a one-byte gap.

findings.failure_path: The byte comparison slices the canonical bytes object before checking the body length. A short result with a correct range size and a large claimed interval therefore copies the entire claimed interval before rejection. Repeated results can spend the hook deadline copying data while holding the conversation lock. The new many-range test supplies an incorrect size and never reaches this line.
findings.smallest_fix: After the UTF-8 start adjustment, reject a body whose length differs from end minus start, then compare using a bounded startswith call or a memoryview. Cover the correct-size, short-body case.

findings.failure_path: The between-writes test changes the pathname's inode. Removing only the cached descriptor's safe_shadow check would leave this test green because the identity comparison still denies the replacement. A hardlink added after the first write keeps that identity unchanged, so the same regression would let the second write publish transcript bytes through both names.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a variant that creates a hardlink to the held shadow between writes while keeping the original name in place. Assert that the second write is denied before the next handler runs, and verify that omitting only cached-descriptor revalidation makes the case fail.

findings.failure_path: The disposition closes the verifier finding by pointing to Local Verification. The frozen packet shows a 56-test focused result, but no current-candidate outcome for make test or the package suite. The attached D1 review identifies ac6c444 as the predecessor. A maintainer cannot establish which required release checks passed on this delta.
findings.smallest_fix: Include the tested revision or tree identity, exact commands, outcomes and skips for the focused, full repository and package suites in the review packet. Mark any outstanding run pending.

findings.failure_path: The packet describes sweep locking, exact-name filtering, age rechecks and truncation, but omits the sweep implementation and its test assertions. It also omits the event lock and cleanup callers. The test register alone cannot establish that an active conversation survives a sweep or that every normal and error exit clears the populated descriptor before unlocking.
findings.smallest_fix: Include the unchanged sweep and event-lifecycle excerpts as review context, together with the assertions for lock-held files, near-miss names, inode preservation and event-end cleanup.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: The three quoted failure paths are closed in the shown code. Rejected ranges share one canonical stream, cached writes recheck the descriptor and pathname, and cleanup returns when the event holds no descriptor. Complete reads can still be missed when two verified chunks finish the same row under different line ranges.

Cached writes check the held file's type, owner and link count before comparing its device and inode with the current name. Descriptor-based cleanup preserves a replacement file. The new test exercises replacement, while the separate link-count check on reuse lacks a regression case.

A malformed short result can still cause a large temporary byte copy during replay. The cache regression checks retained storage and rejects its fixtures at the size check, before the costly comparison.

The replacement and idle-event tests assert observable file contents. The packet supplies no equivalent case for a hardlink added between writes or for a row completed across different ranges. This was a static review of the frozen packet.
The delta adds no operator flag, permission or migration step. Requiring fragments of a row to share one range header imposes a restriction absent from the complete-read acceptance criterion.

This delta changes the in-memory replay cache and retains the existing shadow filename and format. Reverting the delta restores the three prior defects. Reverting all the way to the replace-and-unlink implementation also restores the checkpoint identity problem.

A cached pathname mismatch raises a specific BridgeError, and the replacement test expects a deny. The packet omits the exception-to-verdict and cleanup callers needed to trace other failures, including a missing pathname during lstat.

The profile reports 48 bridge tests, the predecessor reports 53, and this delta reports 56. The named commit belongs to the predecessor. The supplied evidence does not bind the full repository and package suite outcomes to the candidate under review.

Canonical byte comparison protects the load decision against a mismatched body. Descriptor revalidation protects a second write against a replacement or hardlink already present at the check. The plan explicitly scopes out deliberate concurrent interference by the same uid.

The quoted contracts require current-candidate verification for hook changes. The release record marks that obligation fixed, but the frozen packet omits the referenced results. Neither contract is modified.
